title: JSON Schema for a data or config format
when: The user wants to define or document the exact shape of a JSON file, API payload or config so others can produce and check it.
prompt:
Goal: A JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) plus examples describing every field, its type, limits and whether it is required.
Steps:
1. Head: "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema", "$id", "title", "description".
2. Objects: "type": "object", "properties", "required", and "additionalProperties": false for strict formats.
3. Constraints: minLength, maxLength, pattern, minimum, maximum, enum, and "format": "date-time" as documentation.
4. Reuse shared shapes (money, address) through "$defs" and "$ref".
5. Add a top level "version" property; give each field a "description" and "examples".
6. Write example files: minimal valid, full valid, and one invalid with a note saying why.
Quality bar:
- Every property has a type and description.
- One naming convention throughout.
- Dates are ISO 8601 strings; money is integer minor units.
Pitfalls:
- Missing required lists, so every field is optional by accident.
- null, empty string and missing all meaning the same thing.
- Changing a field meaning without bumping version.
Verify:
- [ ] The schema file is valid JSON.
- [ ] Examples match the schema on reading.
- [ ] Each object has required.
- [ ] Repeated shapes live in $defs.
Output: schema/<name>.schema.json and examples/*.json, plus a Fields table in README.

examples.input: document the format of our settings.json
examples.output: settings.schema.json with version, theme enum, fontSize 10 to 32, additionalProperties false, valid and invalid examples
